newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rise as Greenspan tips balance up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rise as Greenspan tips balance up.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed moderately higher Wednesday under a combination of domestic and international influences in which testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan tipped the balance towards the upside.

"It was a totally mixed market. The Wall Street rally allowed us to respect support, but U.S. long bond (30 year Treasury bond) yields and a wobbly peso are still weighing us down," a Mexico City desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 6.8 points, or 0.18 percent, at 3,762.49. Trading volume was restrained at 75.4 million shares.
The broad market did not echo the gain in the IPC. Out of a total of 107 stocks traded, decliners outnumbered gainers by 46 to 39.
Greenspan said Wednesday that the central bank was not out to deflate the stock market by boosting interest rates.
But the Fed chief made clear that the central bank would take account of the level of the stock market, among other factors, in deciding whether to change short-term rates.
The Dow Jones industrial average soared 93.13 points, or 1.36 percent, to close at 6,945.85 points.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts pared an early slide but still closed 1.8 centavos weaker at 8.0150 per dollar.

The most heavily traded gainer was telecoms firm Telmex L class shares, which accounted for 22 percent of shares traded during the session. The L class ended up 14 centavos (2 cents) at 15.54 pesos ($1.94), while Telmex ADRs gained 1/8 to 38-3/4 on Wall Street.
The most heavily traded decliner, meanwhile, was corn flour and tortilla firm Maseca, whose B shares fell 36 centavos (4 cents) to 8.60 pesos ($1.07).
Food firm Grupo Corvi UBL share units topped the decliners' list, falling 42 centavos (5 cents) to 4.50 pesos (56 cents).
Steelmaker Ahmsa was a prominent gainer. Its CPO shares ended up 50 centavos (6 cents) at 17.40 ($2.17).
